la capa más baja de la ionosfera. Solo e: the lowest ionospheric layer. It exists only by day and absorbs the low bands: that is why 80 and 160 m work at night.
la capa más alta y la que hace posible e: the highest layer and the one that makes DX possible: it reflects short waves for thousands of kilometers.

Cada probabilidad de la hora actual se e: Every probability for the current hour is balanced with what the clusters are reporting right now. Spots from the last 45 minutes on that band towards that destination or its area count according to how similar the spotter's path is to yours: same ionospheric reflection area and similar distance. They weigh more when recent, with a good signal and in the same mode as yours: an FT8 spot proves less for SSB, because FT8 gets through with much less signal. With the path confirmed, the figure moves towards what the signal allows, from 35 to 85 %. One hour before or after counts half, and from two hours on only the forecast applies. If you yourself have been heard near that station, it goes up further. Every figure on the platform uses this same measure, except the «VOACAP forecast» layer on the map, which shows the VOACAP forecast alone. Without similar spots VOACAP rules, with one exception: if a lot of DX is being heard on that band from your area and nothing at all from a destination that is normally active, the figure is lowered cautiously, at most by half, because that direction is probably closed.
